deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The previous page prepares the occultation of Aldebaran on 1812 Oct 22, using Moon data from the Connaissance des tems. It computes the Moon's place in a plane through the star and perpendicular to the line of sight to the star (Bessel's later 'fundamental plane'). The coordinates are in arcseconds, scaled by (constant parallax / actual parallax). x points east, parallel to the equator; y points north. The values are given at three Paris times. 'St.W.' is the hour angle of Aldebaran at the Paris meridian; '1'' St.Z.' is one sidereal second.

PART 1: Conjunction from two positions, assuming linear motion.
At hour angle T the Moon is at (x, y); at T+t it is at (x', y'). The Moon moves on a straight line with inclination ζ and speed n (arcsec per sidereal second).
- Direction and speed: tan ζ = (y'-y)/(x'-x), and n = (x'-x)/(t cos ζ) = (y'-y)/(t sin ζ).
- Time Θ when the abscissa is 0 (conjunction in right ascension): Θ = T - x t/(x'-x). The ordinate then is η = y - x tan ζ.
- Conjunction in longitude: the Moon crosses the line through the star in direction 90°+p (the circle of latitude; p is the angle of the ecliptic to the equator-parallel at the star). [Mine] Put the Moon at (nτ cos ζ, η + nτ sin ζ) and require it to equal (-s sin p, s cos p). This gives η sin p + nτ cos(ζ-p) = 0, so the time is Θ - η sin p/(n cos(ζ-p)).

Numbers, using rows 1 and 3 of the previous page:
- x = -5164.5 (log 3.71303n), y = 881.9; x' = 3522.6, y' = 2443.3.
- y'-y = 1561.4 (log 3.19351); x'-x = 8687.1 (log 3.93887).
- t = 24h4'41.3 - 20h4'3.3 = 14438 s (log 4.15951).
- log tan ζ = 9.25464, so ζ = 10°11'22''. log cos ζ = 9.99309, so log((x'-x)/cos ζ) = 3.94579 and log n = 9.78628 (n ≈ 0.611''/s).
- log(t/(x'-x)) = 0.22064; with log x this gives x t/(x'-x) = -8583.6 s = -2h23m3.6s. Hence Θ = 20h4'3.3 + 2h23'3.6 = 22h27'6.9 (hour angle of the star at Paris): conjunction in RA.
- x tan ζ = -928.3, so η = 881.9 + 928.3 = +1810.2 (log 3.25773).
- With p = 9°15'6'': log sin p = 9.20621, C.n = 0.21372, C.cos(ζ-p) = 0.00006. The sum with log η is 2.67772, i.e. 476.1 s.
- Conjunction in longitude = 22h27'6.9 - 7'56.1 = 22h19'10.8.

PART 2: Contact (immersion/emersion) for a place on the Earth.
Let h be the hour angle of the star, φ the corrected (geocentric) latitude, P the corrected horizontal parallax (Earth's radius at the place, in arcseconds), and δ the star's declination.
- (I) Projected position of the observer: a = P cos φ sin h; b = P sin φ cos δ - P cos φ sin δ cos h. In terms of zenith distance z and parallactic angle M: a = P sin z sin M, b = P sin z cos M (the observer's projection lies in direction 90°-M, i.e. toward the projected zenith).
- (II) Relative to the Moon's place at Θ, which is (0, η): b - η = q sin μ, a = q cos μ.
- ρ = the Moon's semidiameter. At contact at time Θ+θ, the line from the projected observer to the projected Moon centre has direction ζ+90°+ν. Hence:
  nθ cos ζ - q cos μ = -ρ sin(ν+ζ)
  nθ sin ζ - q sin μ = ρ cos(ν+ζ)
- [Mine] Eq1·sin ζ - Eq2·cos ζ gives (III): cos ν = q sin(ζ-μ)/ρ.
- [Mine] Eq1·cos ζ + Eq2·sin ζ gives (IV): nθ = q cos(ζ-μ) - ρ sin ν. Equivalently θ = q cos(ζ-μ+ν)/(n cos ν) = (q/n) cos(ζ-μ) - (q/n) sin(ζ-μ) tan ν.
- (III) gives two values ±ν. The one with sin ν > 0 gives the smaller θ, i.e. the immersion; the other gives the emersion.
- The next page interprets the angles geometrically and works an example for Göttingen.
errors: No substantive error in the derivations; all logarithmic arithmetic checks to the last unit (my small slip: 3.94578 vs Gauss's 3.94579 for log((x'-x)/cos ζ), which is rounding).

In line I the second alternative form appears as 'P cos z cos M'. Geometrically (and by the next page's statement that 90-M is the direction toward point 3) it must be P sin z cos M, the projected distance being P sin z. This is either a slip of the pen or a misreading.

Linear interpolation over 4 sidereal hours is an approximation, but it is checked by the middle row of the previous page: the linear prediction at t/2 is (-820.9, 1662.6) against the tabulated (-820.7, 1662.5), so the error is negligible.

Consistency check (mine): the zero of the ecliptic x-coordinate on the previous page, by linear interpolation, falls at T + 8107.5 s. This equals Θ - 476.1 s exactly, confirming the formula for conjunction in longitude and its sign.

results.what: Reduction of the Moon's relative motion in the plane perpendicular to the star to a straight line (inclination ζ, hourly motion n), with time of closest-axis passage Θ and minimum ordinate η; conjunction in RA and in longitude
results.modern_name: Linear-motion reduction in the fundamental plane (Besselian-element style occultation prediction)
results.usually_credited_to: Orthographic projection methods: Lagrange, Lambert, Du Séjour (18th c.); systematic fundamental-plane occultation theory: F. W. Bessel (1820s–1842)

results.what: Observer coordinates in the fundamental plane: a = P cos φ sin h, b = P(sin φ cos δ - cos φ sin δ cos h) = (P sin z sin M, P sin z cos M)
results.modern_name: Besselian observer coordinates ξ, η (rho cos φ' sin H, rho(sin φ' cos d - cos φ' sin d cos H))

results.what: Contact condition: cos ν = q sin(ζ-μ)/ρ and nθ = q cos(ζ-μ) - ρ sin ν; sign of sin ν separates immersion and emersion
results.modern_name: Bessel's contact equations for occultations/eclipses (the 'sin ψ / cos ψ' equation for times of contact)
results.usually_credited_to: Bessel; also Lagrange-type eclipse projection formulas

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working computation for the 1812 Aldebaran occultation. It uses a plane through the star perpendicular to its direction, Moon coordinates scaled by the parallax ratio, Besselian-type observer coordinates and a clean contact equation. This is essentially the scheme Bessel later systematised and published (1820s–1842). Projection methods for eclipses and occultations already existed (Lagrange, Lambert, Du Séjour), and Gauss's competence here is unsurprising. Still, a fully fundamental-plane occultation algorithm by Gauss around 1812, predating Bessel's publications, is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major priority discovery.

transcription_corrections: 'δ in AR' and 'δ in Long.' should read '☌ in AR' and '☌ in Long.' (conjunction symbol, not declination).
'Halbmesser C = ρ' should read 'Halbmesser ☾ = ρ' (semidiameter of the Moon).
'St.W.' means Stundenwinkel (hour angle of the star at Paris), not a time label 'St.W.' of another kind.
Heading line: 'wo Stundenwinkel des Sterns h, verbesserte Polhöhe φ, verbesserte Horizontalparallaxe P' — the symbol φ after Polhöhe is implied or illegible.
In I, the second alternative form '= P cos z cos M' should mathematically be 'P sin z cos M'; possibly a misreading, possibly Gauss's slip.
In IV the first numerator is cos(ζ-μ+ν) (partly blotted in the image); the later '-' signs are blotted but must be minus.
(Next page, for context) 'ν = 128.27.20' is inconsistent with log cos ν = 9.76348n and log cos(ζ-μ+ν) = 9.94872. It should be 125°27'20''.
